title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — पुरुषोत्तमयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 15: The Supreme Person
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/पुरुषोत्तमयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t:
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् ।
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
sentences.tr:
ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śākham aśvattham prāhuḥ avyayam |
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yaḥ tam veda sa veda-vit ||

morph.gloss: upward, above (first member of ūrdhva-mūlam)
root (ūrdhva-mūlam: 'having its root above, upward-rooted', bahuvrīhi, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with aśvattham)
below, downward (adhaḥ: first member of adhaḥ-śākham; visarga retained before ś-, one of two options Pāṇini allows before a sibilant)
branch (adhaḥ-śākham: 'having its branches below, downward-branched', bahuvrīhi, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with aśvattham)
the aśvattha, the sacred fig tree (Ficus religiosa) (acc. sg. masc., object of prāhuḥ; the three words are simply written joined, each final -m unaffected before the next sound)
to declare, proclaim, call (prāhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used with an indefinite subject, 'they call, they declare'; -uḥ+a-→-ur a-)
imperishable, undecaying (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with aśvattham, predicate complement of prāhuḥ)
a Vedic hymn, a sacred verse; also 'a meter' (nom. pl. neut., predicate)
whose, of which (gen. sg. neut., referring to the aśvattha)
leaf (nom. pl. neut., subject)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative, subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-)
it, him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of veda, referring to the tree)
to know (veda: perfect 3rd sg. used as present, 'knows')
he (sa: nom. sg. masc., subject, correlative)
the Veda (first compound member)
knowing, a knower (agent noun from vid; veda-vit: 'a knower of the Veda', nom. sg. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: Upward-rooted, downward-branched, the aśvattha they call imperishable; whose leaves [are] the sacred hymns — who knows it, he [is] a knower of the Veda.
sentences.i: They speak of an imperishable aśvattha tree with its root above and its branches below, the hymns of the Veda its leaves; whoever knows this tree is one who truly knows the Veda.
sentences.n: Chapter 15 opens with no question from Arjuna; Kṛṣṇa continues speaking directly from chapter 14's close, at once introducing the celebrated image that runs through verses 1-4: the cosmic aśvattha (the sacred fig, Ficus religiosa) turned upside down, its root growing ūrdhvam, 'upward', and its branches adhaḥ, 'downward' — a figure the tradition (Śaṅkara) reads as saṃsāra, the tree of transmigratory existence rooted in the unmanifest above and branching down into the visible world, and already found at Kaṭha Upaniṣad 6.1's ūrdhva-mūlo 'vāk-śākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ. Chandāṃsi, 'the Vedic hymns', are its parṇāni, 'leaves' — an ornament and a protection, as leaves are to a tree, rather than the tree's essence, so that knowing the tree itself, not only its leaves, is what makes one a veda-vit, 'a knower of the Veda' in the fullest sense. Sandhi: ūrdhvamūlam adhaḥśākham aśvattham are three appositive words simply written joined, each final -m unaffected before what follows; prāhur avyayam is prāhuḥ+avyayam (-uḥ+a-→-ur a-); yas taṃ is yaḥ+tam (-aḥ+t-→-as t-).

sentences.t:
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा ।
गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः ।
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसंततानि ।
कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥
sentences.tr:
adhaḥ ca ūrdhvam prasṛtāḥ tasya śākhāḥ |
guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ viṣaya-pravālāḥ |
adhaḥ ca mūlāni anusaṃtatāni |
karma-anubandhīni manuṣya-loke ||

morph.gloss: below, downward (adhaḥ: adverb; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and (ca+ūrdhvam→cordhvam, a+ū→o)
above, upward (ūrdhvam: adverb)
spread forth, extended (prasṛta: past participle, nom. pl. fem., predicate, agreeing with śākhāḥ; -āḥ+t-→-ās t-)
its (tasya: gen. sg., referring to the tree of verse 1)

branch (nom. pl. fem., subject; the visarga of -āḥ is silently elided before the following voiced g- of guṇapravṛddhāḥ, carried across the pāda break — a pattern distinct from the more familiar -aḥ→-o, and recurring wherever a plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound)
quality; the guṇas, kept untranslated in the idiomatic rendering per convention (first compound member)

grown, increased (pravṛddha: past participle, guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ: 'nourished/increased by the guṇas', nom. pl. fem., agreeing with śākhāḥ; its own -āḥ likewise elides before the voiced v- of viṣaya- that follows)
a sense-object, an object of the senses (first compound member)
sprout, new shoot, tender twig (viṣaya-pravālāḥ: 'having sense-objects as their new shoots', nom. pl. fem., agreeing with śākhāḥ)
below, downward (adhaḥ: adverb; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and
root (mūlāni: nom. pl. neut., subject; -i+a-→-y a-)
stretched out, extended continuously (anusaṃtata: past participle, nom. pl. neut., predicate, agreeing with mūlāni)
action (first compound member; karma+anubandhīni→karmānubandhīni, a+a→ā)
binding to, entailing (from anu-bandh, 'to bind, entail consequences'; karma-anubandhīni: 'bound to action, entailing the consequences of action', nom. pl. neut., agreeing with mūlāni)
man, human being (first compound member)
world (manuṣya-loka: 'the human world', loc. sg.)

sentences.l: Below and above spread its branches, nourished-by-the-guṇas, having-sense-objects-as-sprouts; and below, roots stretched-out continuously, bound-to-action, in-the-world-of-men.
sentences.i: Its branches spread both downward and upward, nourished by the guṇas, putting out the sense objects as their tender shoots; and below, its roots stretch on without a break, binding one to action in the human world.
sentences.n: The tree-image continues (through verse 4): its śākhāḥ, 'branches', spread both adhaḥ and ūrdhvam, 'below and above', through every level of existence, guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ, 'nourished by the guṇas' (sattva, rajas and tamas of chapter 14, kept untranslated per convention), and putting forth viṣaya-pravālāḥ, 'sense-objects as their sprouts' — the branches' new growth is exactly what tempts and traps the senses. Secondary mūlāni, 'roots', spread continuously downward too, anubandhīni, 'entailing, binding one to', karman, 'action', in manuṣya-loke, 'the human world' — the ordinary world of ritual and worldly action, as against the tree's unseen root above. Sandhi: adhaścordhvaṃ packs adhaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) and ca+ūrdhvam (a+ū→o); prasṛtāstasya is prasṛtāḥ+tasya (-āḥ+t-→-ās t-); śākhā (visarga-less at the pāda's end) and guṇapravṛddhā (likewise) both show the visarga of an -āḥ ending silently dropping before a following voiced consonant (g-, v- respectively) — a pattern distinct from the more familiar -aḥ→-o of a short-a ending, and one that recurs through this chapter wherever a fem./masc. plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound; adhaśca is adhaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-); mūlānyanusaṃtatāni is mūlāni+anusaṃtatāni (-i+a-→-y a-); karmānubandhīni is karma+anubandhīni (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते ।
नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा ।
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल- ।
मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥
sentences.tr:
na rūpam asya iha tathā upalabhyate |
na antaḥ na ca ādiḥ na ca saṃpratiṣṭhā |
aśvattham enam su-virūḍha-mūla(m)- |
(-m) asaṅga-śastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā ||

morph.gloss: not
form, shape (rūpam: nom. sg. neut., subject; simply joined with asya, -m unaffected before the vowel)
its (asya: gen. sg., referring to the tree)
here, in this world (asya+iha→asyeha, a+i→e)
thus, in that way (adverb; tathā+upalabhyate→tathopalabhyate, ā+u→o)
to perceive, apprehend (upalabhyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is apprehended')
not (na+antaḥ→nāntaḥ, a+a→ā)
end (antaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
not
and (ca+ādiḥ→cādiḥ, a+ā→ā)
beginning (ādiḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -iḥ+n-→-ir n-)
not, nor (repeated)
and
foundation, resting-place, stable basis (nom. sg. fem., subject)
the aśvattha tree (acc. sg. masc., object of chittvā, resuming the tree of verses 1-2)
this (enam: acc. sg. masc., emphatic, agreeing with aśvattham; simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
well, thoroughly (prefix, first member)
grown up, sprung up (virūḍha: past participle, second member, 'well-grown')

root (third member; su-virūḍha-mūlam: 'having well-grown roots', bahuvrīhi, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with aśvattham enam — uniquely in this chapter the word's final -m is carried, by ordinary sandhi with the following vowel, onto the far side of the pāda break; this is an authentic feature of the transmitted text, reproduced here exactly as given and not a misprint — see the note)
root (this token opens with the -m that completes the previous line's mūlam, fused by sandhi with the following vowel and carried across the line break; -m+a-→ simply joined)
non-attachment, freedom from attachment (first compound member of this word)
a weapon, a blade (asaṅga-śastra: 'the weapon of non-attachment', instr. sg.)
firm, strong (instr. sg. neut., agreeing with śastreṇa)
to cut, sever (chittvā: gerund, 'having cut down')

sentences.l: Its form is not perceived here in that way; nor an end, nor also a beginning, nor a foundation; this aśvattha, with-well-grown-roots, having cut with the firm weapon of non-attachment —
sentences.i: Its true form cannot be perceived here as it is; it has no end, no beginning, and no stable ground. Having cut down this aśvattha with its deep-grown roots, with the firm weapon of non-attachment —
sentences.n: This denies that the cosmic tree's rūpam, 'form' (its ultimate shape, as against its familiar appearance), can be grasped as it really is, and further denies it has anta, ādi, or saṃpratiṣṭhā — 'end', 'beginning', or 'foundation' — a set of negations recalling how the self/brahman is elsewhere described as beginningless and endless (e.g. 2.20's ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yam purāṇo); saṃsāra, pictured as this tree, has no discoverable starting point or bottom from within it. The sentence begun here runs on into verse 4: aśvattham enaṃ suvirūḍha-mūlam, 'this aśvattha with its roots grown deep and strong', must be cut down asaṅga-śastreṇa dṛḍhena, 'with the firm weapon of non-attachment' (asaṅga, echoing chapters 2-3's teaching that attachment, saṅga, is what binds action). Uniquely in this chapter (indeed in the whole poem), the compound suvirūḍha-mūlam is split by the pāda break itself: the source text (reproduced exactly here) ends this line with सुविरूढमूल- and begins the next with मसङ्गशस्त्रेण, so that the word's final -m, fused by ordinary sandhi with the following asaṅga-, falls on the far side of the line/word-token boundary — an authentic feature of the transmitted text, not a misprint, and so left untouched. Sandhi: rūpamasyeha packs rūpam+asya (simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel) and asya+iha (a+i→e); tathopalabhyate is tathā+upalabhyate (ā+u→o); nānto is na+antaḥ (a+a→ā), whose own -aḥ before n-→-o; cādirna packs ca+ādiḥ (a+ā→ā) and ādiḥ+na (-iḥ+n-→-ir n-).

sentences.t:
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं ।
यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः ।
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये ।
यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥
sentences.tr:
tataḥ padam tat parimārgitavyam |
yasmin gatāḥ na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |
tam eva ca ādyam puruṣam prapadye |
yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī ||

morph.gloss: from that, then, thence (adverb)
place, state, station (nom. sg. neut., subject of the passive gerundive parimārgitavyam)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., in apposition with padam, 'that [state]')
to seek out, track down (parimārgitavya: gerundive, 'is to be sought out', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with padam)
which (yasmin: loc. sg. neut. relative, 'into which, wherein')
to go (gata: past participle, gatāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, 'having gone [there]'; simply written joined, the nasal of yasmin unaffected before the consonant g-)
not
to turn back, return (nivartanti: present 3rd pl., 'they return')
again, once more (adverb)
that, him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of prapadye, referring forward to puruṣam)
indeed, alone
and (ca+ādyam→cādyam, a+ā→ā)
primal, original, first (ādyam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam)
the Person (acc. sg. masc., object of prapadye)
to take refuge in, resort to (prapadye: present middle 1st sg., 'I take refuge in')
from whom, from which (adverb/relative, referring to puruṣam)
activity, outgoing tendency, active engagement (nom. sg. fem., subject)
spread forth, issued forth (prasṛtā: past participle, nom. sg. fem., predicate, agreeing with pravṛttiḥ)
ancient, primeval (purāṇī: nom. sg. fem., agreeing with pravṛttiḥ)

sentences.l: Thence, that state must be sought, into which, having gone, they do not return again; that very primal Person I take refuge in, from whom the ancient activity has issued forth.
sentences.i: Then that state must be sought out, from which those who reach it never return; I take refuge in that same primal Person, from whom this age-old outgoing activity first issued.
sentences.n: This completes the sentence begun in verses 3-4 (chittvā, 'having cut', governs what follows): once the tree of saṃsāra is felled with non-attachment, tataḥ, 'thence', one must seek out padam, 'that state', from which yasmin gatāḥ na nivartanti bhūyaḥ, 'having gone into which they do not return again' — the same promise made of liberation at 8.21's yaṃ prāpya na nivartante. That state is identified with tam eva ca ādyam puruṣam, 'that very primal Person' (puruṣa, translated throughout this pipeline as 'the Person', following the convention set at chapters 8, 10-11 and 13, rather than left untranslated), in whom Kṛṣṇa says he takes refuge (prapadye) — speaking, in effect, of himself in the third person as yataḥ, 'the one from whom', purāṇī pravṛttiḥ, 'the ancient/primeval activity', has issued forth, recalling the cosmogony of 14.3-4's seed placed in the great brahman. Sandhi: yasmingatā is yasmin+gatāḥ, simply written joined (the nasal unaffected before the consonant g-); cādyaṃ is ca+ādyam (a+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा ।
अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः ।
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै- ।
र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
sentences.tr:
nirmāna-mohāḥ jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ |
adhyātma-nityāḥ vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ |
dvandvaiḥ vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñaiḥ- |
(-r) gacchanti amūḍhāḥ padam avyayam tat ||

morph.gloss: free from pride, without self-conceit (nirmāna: first member of the bahuvrīhi)

delusion (nirmāna-moha: 'free from pride and delusion', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; the visarga of the plural -āḥ is elided before the following voiced j- of jitasaṅgadoṣāḥ, as at verse 2's śākhā and guṇapravṛddhā)
conquered, overcome (jita: past participle, first member)
attachment (second member)
fault, flaw (jita-saṅga-doṣa: 'having conquered the fault of attachment', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc.; its own -āḥ elides before the following voiced a- of adhyātmanityāḥ)
pertaining to the self, the inner self (adhyātma: first compound member, adhi+ātman→adhyātma, the same term named at 8.3)
constant, ever intent on (adhyātma-nitya: 'ever intent on the inner self', nom. pl. masc.; its -āḥ elides before the voiced v- of vinivṛttakāmāḥ)
turned back, ceased, withdrawn (vinivṛtta: past participle, first member)
desire (vinivṛtta-kāma: 'whose desires have ceased', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject)
a pair of opposites, a duality (dvandvaiḥ: instr. pl., 'by/from the dualities')
freed, released (vimukta: past participle, vimuktāḥ: nom. pl. masc., 'freed'; -aiḥ+v-→-air v-)
happiness, pleasure (first compound member)
pain, suffering (second member)

name, designation (sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñā: 'called/designated pleasure and pain', instr. pl., in apposition with dvandvaiḥ — as at verse 3, the source splits this compound exactly at the point where its final visarga fuses by sandhi with the following gacchanti, carrying an 'r' onto the next printed line; reproduced here as given, not a misprint — see the note)
to go (gacchanti: present 3rd pl., 'they go'; its initial r completes the sandhi of saṃjñaiḥ from the previous line, -aiḥ+g-→-air g-; gacchanti+amūḍhāḥ→gacchantyamūḍhāḥ, -i+a-→-y a-)
undeluded, unconfused (amūḍhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, in apposition with all the preceding predicate adjectives)
place, state (acc. sg. neut., object of gacchanti)
imperishable (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with padam)
that (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with padam, resuming verse 4's tat parimārgitavyam)

sentences.l: Free-from-pride-and-delusion, having-conquered-the-fault-of-attachment, ever-intent-on-the-inner-self, their-desires-withdrawn, freed from the dualities called pleasure-and-pain, the-undeluded go to that imperishable state.
sentences.i: Free from pride and delusion, having conquered the taint of attachment, ever fixed on the inner self, their desires stilled, freed from the dualities known as pleasure and pain — the undeluded reach that imperishable state.
sentences.n: This continues the sentence begun in verses 3-4, now describing, in a long run of compounds, those who actually reach the imperishable padam named at the end of verse 4: they are nirmāna-mohāḥ, 'free of pride and delusion'; jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ, 'having conquered the fault of attachment' (recalling the saṅga just cut away by the asaṅga-śastra of verse 3); adhyātma-nityāḥ, 'ever intent on the inner self' (adhyātma named already at 8.3); vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ, 'their desires withdrawn'; and dvandvaiḥ vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñaiḥ, 'freed from the dualities called pleasure and pain' (the same confusion of opposites named at 7.27-28). As at verse 3, the source splits a compound across the pāda break: sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñaiḥ, at the line's end, is completed by the -r- that begins the next line (from -aiḥ+g-→-air g-, before gacchanti), again an authentic feature of the transmitted text reproduced here as given. Amūḍhāḥ, 'the undeluded', is the subject of gacchanti, 'go' (understood also with all the preceding predicate adjectives), reaching padam avyayam tat, 'that imperishable state' — padam having been named in verse 4, now qualified avyayam, 'imperishable', for the first time. Sandhi: gacchantyamūḍhāḥ is gacchanti+amūḍhāḥ (-i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t:
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
sentences.tr:
na tat bhāsayate sūryaḥ na śaśāṅkaḥ na pāvakaḥ |
yat gatvā na nivartante tat dhāma paramam mama ||

morph.gloss: not
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of bhāsayate, referring to the padam of verse 5; -t+bh-→-d bh-)
to illumine, shine upon (causative; bhāsayate: present middle 3rd sg. used in an active sense, 'illumines')
the sun (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
not
hare (first compound member)
mark, spot (śaśa-aṅka: 'the hare-marked one', i.e. the moon, nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
not
fire (nom. sg. masc., subject)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object of gatvā, referring to the imperishable state; -t+g-→-d g-)
to go (gatvā: gerund, 'having gone [to which]')
not
to return (nivartante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they return')
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t+dh-→-d dh-)
abode, seat, glory (dhāma: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
highest, supreme (paramam: nom. sg. neut., agreeing with dhāma)
I (mama: gen. sg., 'my')

sentences.l: That, the sun illumines not, nor the moon, nor fire; having gone to which they do not return — that [is] my supreme abode.
sentences.i: Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire illumines that place; having reached it, none return — that is my supreme abode.
sentences.n: This describes the imperishable padam of verses 4-5 further: it is beyond illumination by any of the great luminaries — sūrya, 'the sun', śaśāṅka, 'the moon' (literally 'hare-marked', from the mark seen on its face), and pāvaka, 'fire' — because it is itself self-luminous, closely echoing Kaṭha Upaniṣad 5.15 and Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 6.14's na tatra sūryo bhāti na candra-tārakam. Kṛṣṇa now names it directly as tat dhāma paramam mama, 'that, my supreme abode', identifying the destination of verses 4-5 as his own. Sandhi: sūryo na is sūryaḥ+na (-aḥ before n-→-o); śaśāṅko na is śaśāṅkaḥ+na (-aḥ before n-→-o); yad gatvā is yat+gatvā (-t+g-→-d g-); tad dhāma is tat+dhāma (-t+dh-→-d dh-).

sentences.t:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
sentences.tr:
mama eva aṃśaḥ jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi prakṛti-sthāni karṣati ||

morph.gloss: I (mama: gen. sg. 'my')
indeed (mama+eva→mamaiva, a+e→ai)
a part, a portion, a fragment (aṃśaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before j-→-o)
a living being, a soul (first compound member)
world (jīva-loka: 'the world of living beings', loc. sg.)
living, life (first compound member)
become (bhūta: past participle, jīva-bhūta: 'become a living being, a jīva', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
eternal, everlasting (nom. sg. masc., agreeing with aṃśaḥ)
mind (first compound member; visarga retained before ṣ-, as at verse 1's adhaḥśākham)
sixth (manaḥ-ṣaṣṭha: 'with the mind as sixth', bahuvrīhi describing indriyāṇi; manaḥṣaṣṭhāni+indriyāṇi→manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi, -i+i-→-ī-, vowel lengthening)
a sense-organ, a faculty (indriyāṇi: acc. pl. neut., object of karṣati)
nature (first compound member)
abiding in, situated in (prakṛti-sthāni: 'seated in nature', acc. pl. neut., agreeing with indriyāṇi)
to draw, drag (karṣati: present 3rd sg., 'draws [to itself]')

sentences.l: An eternal fragment of me alone, in the world of living beings, becomes a living soul; it draws to itself the senses, with mind as sixth, abiding in nature.
sentences.i: An eternal fragment of myself alone becomes, in the world of living beings, an individual soul, and draws to itself the senses — with the mind as the sixth — that are seated in nature.
sentences.n: This opens a new section (through verse 11) that turns from the impersonal tree-image to the individual jīva, 'living soul': it is Kṛṣṇa's own aṃśaḥ, 'a part, a fragment', sanātanaḥ, 'eternal', though appearing as jīva-bhūtaḥ, 'become a living being' — the claim, taken up by later tradition as the doctrine of the jīva as an aṃśa of Īśvara, that the individual self differs from the Supreme not in kind but only as a portion embodied. Such a soul karṣati, 'draws' (or 'drags along'), the indriyāṇi, 'senses' — manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhāni, 'with mind as the sixth' (the five sense-organs plus manas, counted as a sixth, exactly as at 2.67's account of the senses dragging the mind) — which are themselves prakṛti-sthāni, 'seated in nature', not in the soul itself. Sandhi: mamaivāṃśo packs mama+eva (a+e→ai) and aṃśaḥ+jīvaloke (-aḥ before j-→-o); manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi packs manaḥ+ṣaṣṭhāni (visarga retained before ṣ-, as already at verse 1's adhaḥśākham) and ṣaṣṭhāni+indriyāṇi (-i+i-→-ī-, vowel lengthening of like vowels).

sentences.t:
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥
sentences.tr:
śarīram yat avāpnoti yat ca api utkrāmati īśvaraḥ |
gṛhītvā etāni saṃyāti vāyuḥ gandhān iva āśayāt ||

morph.gloss: body (acc. sg. neut., object of avāpnoti)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object, referring to śarīram; -t+a-→-d a-, a final stop voiced before a vowel)
to obtain, acquire (avāpnoti: present 3rd sg., 'obtains')
which, and (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, further object with ca; -t+c-→-c c-)
and
also, even (ca+api→cāpi, a+a→ā)
to go forth, depart (utkrāmati: present 3rd sg., 'departs'; api+utkrāmati→cāpyutkrāmati, -i+u-→-y u-)
the lord, the ruling one — here the individual soul as controller of its own body and senses (nom. sg. masc., subject; utkrāmati+īśvaraḥ→utkrāmatīśvaraḥ, -i+ī-→-ī-)
to seize, take hold of (gṛhītvā: gerund, 'having taken hold of')
these (etāni: acc. pl. neut., object of gṛhītvā, referring to the senses of verse 7; gṛhītvā+etāni→gṛhītvaitāni, ā+e→ai)
to go along with, proceed (saṃyāti: present 3rd sg., 'proceeds')
wind, air (vāyuḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject of the simile; -uḥ+g-→-ur g-)
scent, odor (gandhān: acc. pl. masc., understood object of an implied verb of carrying, completing the simile; simply joined with iva)
like, as (particle of comparison)
a receptacle, a resting-place (e.g. a flower) (āśayāt: abl. sg., 'from [its] resting-place'; iva+āśayāt→ivāśayāt, a+ā→ā)

sentences.l: The body which he obtains, and which the lord departs from, having seized these [senses], he goes along [with them] — as the wind [carries] scents from their resting-place.
sentences.i: As the lord — the embodied soul — takes up a body, and as it departs from one, it takes these senses along and goes on its way, just as the wind carries scents away from their resting place, a flower.
sentences.n: This describes how the jīva of verse 7 passes from body to body: īśvaraḥ (here 'the lord, the ruling one' — the individual soul as controller of its own body and senses, not the Supreme Lord) yat śarīram avāpnoti, 'the body it acquires', and yat [śarīrāt] ca api utkrāmati, 'and [the body] it also departs from', in both cases takes gṛhītvā, 'having seized', etāni, 'these' [the senses named in verse 7] along with it, saṃyāti, 'proceeding on', vāyuḥ gandhān iva āśayāt, 'like the wind carrying scents away from their resting place' — a well-known simile, already glossed this way by Śaṅkara, of the subtle senses borne along by the departing soul as a breeze carries a flower's fragrance from the flower itself. Sandhi: yadavāpnoti is yat+avāpnoti (-t+a-→-d a-, a stop voiced before a vowel); yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ packs yat+ca (-t+c-→-c c-, assimilation), ca+api (a+a→ā), api+utkrāmati (-i+u-→-y u-), and utkrāmati+īśvaraḥ (-i+ī-→-ī-, vowel lengthening); gṛhītvaitāni is gṛhītvā+etāni (ā+e→ai); vāyurgandhāniva is vāyuḥ+gandhān (-uḥ+g-→-ur g-), gandhān+iva simply joined; ivāśayāt is iva+āśayāt (a+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥
sentences.tr:
śrotram cakṣuḥ sparśanam ca rasanam ghrāṇam eva ca |
adhiṣṭhāya manaḥ ca ayam viṣayān upasevate ||

morph.gloss: the ear, hearing (acc. sg. neut., object of adhiṣṭhāya)
the eye, sight (acc. sg. neut., object)
touch, the sense of touch (acc. sg. neut., object)
and
taste, the sense of taste (acc. sg. neut., object)
smell, the sense of smell (acc. sg. neut., object; simply joined with eva, -m unaffected before the vowel)
indeed, too
and
to preside over, take control of (adhiṣṭhāya: gerund, 'having taken control of')
the mind (manaḥ: acc. sg. neut., additional object of adhiṣṭhāya; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc., subject, referring to the soul; ca+ayam→cāyam, a+a→ā)
a sense-object (viṣayān: acc. pl. masc., object of upasevate)
to resort to, enjoy, partake of (upasevate: present middle 3rd sg., 'partakes of')

sentences.l: Having taken control of the ear, the eye, touch, and taste, and smell too, and the mind, this [soul] partakes of the sense-objects.
sentences.i: Taking control of the ear, the eye, touch, taste, and smell, and the mind as well, this soul enjoys the objects of the senses.
sentences.n: This continues verse 8's description of the embodying soul, naming the six faculties it governs (adhiṣṭhāya, 'having taken control of, presiding over'): the five senses — śrotra (hearing), cakṣus (sight), sparśana (touch), rasana (taste), ghrāṇa (smell) — plus manas, 'the mind', the sixth already named at verse 7's manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhāni; through them ayam, 'this [soul]', upasevate, 'partakes of, resorts to', viṣayān, 'the sense-objects'. Sandhi: ghrāṇameva is ghrāṇam+eva, simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel; manaścāyam packs manaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) and ca+ayam (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
sentences.tr:
utkrāmantam sthitam vā api bhuñjānam vā guṇa-anvitam |
vimūḍhāḥ na anupaśyanti paśyanti jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ ||

morph.gloss: departing, going forth (utkrāmant: present participle, utkrāmantam: acc. sg. masc., object of anupaśyanti/paśyanti, referring to the soul)
abiding, remaining (sthita: past participle, acc. sg. masc., 'remaining [in the body]')
or (vā+api→vāpi, ā+a→ā)
also, even (emphatic)
enjoying, partaking of (bhuñjāna: present middle participle, acc. sg. masc., 'enjoying [the sense-objects]')
or
the guṇas, kept untranslated per convention (first compound member; guṇa+anvitam→guṇānvitam, a+a→ā)
accompanied by, united with (from anu-i; guṇa-anvita: 'united with the guṇas', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with the soul)
deluded, confused (vimūḍha: past participle, vimūḍhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; the visarga elides before the following voiced n- of na, as at verse 2's śākhā and verse 5's nirmānamohāḥ)
not
to perceive, see (anupaśyanti: present 3rd pl., 'they perceive'; na+anupaśyanti→nānupaśyanti, a+a→ā)
to see (paśyanti: present 3rd pl., 'they see')
knowledge (first compound member)
eye (jñāna-cakṣus: 'those whose eye is knowledge, those possessing the eye of knowledge', nom. pl. masc., subject)

sentences.l: [Whether] departing, or remaining, or enjoying [the senses], united-with-the-guṇas — the deluded do not perceive [it]; those-with-the-eye-of-knowledge perceive [it].
sentences.i: The deluded do not perceive the soul as it departs, or stays, or enjoys the senses, united with the guṇas; but those who have the eye of knowledge do perceive it.
sentences.n: This closes the section on the embodied soul (verses 7-10) by contrasting two kinds of perceiver: the vimūḍhāḥ, 'the deluded', na anupaśyanti, 'do not perceive', the soul in any of its states — utkrāmantam, 'departing' (as at verse 8), sthitam, 'remaining [in the body]', or bhuñjānam, 'enjoying [the sense-objects]' (as at verse 9), guṇa-anvitam, 'joined with the guṇas' (the very guṇas whose interplay chapter 14 described) — while jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ, 'those who have the eye of knowledge' (a recurring Gītā image, cf. 13.34's jñāna-cakṣuṣā), paśyanti, 'do perceive' it, echoing 13.34's teaching that only knowledge, not the physical eye, discerns the field from its knower. Sandhi: vāpi is vā+api (ā+a→ā); guṇānvitam is guṇa+anvitam (a+a→ā); nānupaśyanti is na+anupaśyanti (a+a→ā); vimūḍhā, at the pāda's end, shows the same -āḥ elision before a following voiced consonant (n- of na anupaśyanti, across the pāda break) already noted at verse 2.

sentences.t:
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ।
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥
sentences.tr:
yatantaḥ yoginaḥ ca enam paśyanti ātmani avasthitam |
yatantaḥ api akṛta-ātmānaḥ na enam paśyanti acetasaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to strive, make effort (yatant: present participle, yatantaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ before y-→-o)
a yogin (yoginaḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition with yatantaḥ; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and
this, it (enam: acc. sg. masc., object of paśyanti, referring to the self; ca+enam→cainam, a+e→ai)
to see (paśyanti: present 3rd pl.; paśyanti+ātmani→paśyantyātmani, -i+ā-→-y ā-)
the self (ātmani: loc. sg., 'in the self')
abiding, situated (avasthita: past participle, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with enam; ātmani+avasthitam→ātmanyavasthitam, -i+a-→-y a-)
to strive, make effort (yatant: present participle, yatantaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha)
even, also (api+akṛtātmānaḥ→apyakṛtātmānaḥ, -i+a-→-y a-)
one whose self is unaccomplished, unperfected (bahuvrīhi; akṛtātmānaḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition with yatantaḥ; -aḥ before n-→-o)
not (na+enam→nainam, a+e→ai)
him, it (enam: acc. sg. masc., object of paśyanti)
to see (paśyanti: present 3rd pl.; paśyanti+acetasaḥ→paśyantyacetasaḥ, -i+a-→-y a-)
unintelligent, lacking discernment (acetasaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject)

sentences.l: Striving yogins perceive it, abiding within the self; but, even striving, the-unaccomplished, thoughtless [seekers] do not perceive it.
sentences.i: Yogins who strive perceive it dwelling within the self; but the unaccomplished, lacking discernment, do not perceive it, even though they strive.
sentences.n: This contrasts two kinds of strivers, sharpening verse 10's contrast of the deluded and the discerning: yatantaḥ yoginaḥ, 'yogins who strive', do paśyanti, 'perceive', enam [the soul] ātmani avasthitam, 'abiding within the self'; but even yatantaḥ api, 'even those who strive', if they are akṛta-ātmānaḥ, 'whose selves are unaccomplished, unperfected' (whose discipline has not yet borne fruit) and acetasaḥ, 'lacking discernment', na paśyanti, 'do not perceive' it — effort alone, without the ripening of insight, does not suffice, a qualification already implied at 6.44-45's account of the yogin still in training. Sandhi: yatanto is yatantaḥ, -aḥ before y-→-o; yoginaścainaṃ packs yoginaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) and ca+enam (a+e→ai); paśyantyātmanyavasthitam packs paśyanti+ātmani (-i+ā-→-y ā-) and ātmani+avasthitam (-i+a-→-y a-); yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno packs yatantaḥ+api (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha), api+akṛtātmānaḥ (-i+a-→-y a-), and akṛtātmānaḥ+na (-aḥ before n-→-o); nainaṃ is na+enam (a+e→ai); paśyantyacetasaḥ is paśyanti+acetasaḥ (-i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t:
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् ।
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yat āditya-gatam tejaḥ jagat bhāsayate akhilam |
yat ca candramasi yat ca agnau tat tejaḥ viddhi māmakam ||

morph.gloss: which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, subject; yat+āditya→yadāditya, -t+ā-→-d ā-)
the sun (first compound member)
to go (gata: past participle, 'residing in' — āditya-gata: 'residing in the sun', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with tejaḥ)
light, radiance, splendor (nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ before j-→-o)
the world (acc. sg. neut., object of bhāsayate; jagat+bhāsayate→jagadbhāsayate, -t+bh-→-d bh-)
to illumine (causative; bhāsayate: present middle 3rd sg. used actively, 'illumines')
whole, entire (akhilam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat; bhāsayate+akhilam→bhāsayate'khilam, -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)
which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, continuing the subject; -t+c-→-c c-)
and
the moon (candramasi: loc. sg., 'in the moon')
which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative; -t+c-→-c c-)
and (ca+agnau→cāgnau, a+a→ā)
fire (agnau: loc. sg., 'in fire')
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of viddhi; -t+t-→-t t-)
radiance, light (tejaḥ: acc. sg. neut., in apposition with tat; -aḥ before v-→-o)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!')
mine, belonging to me (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with tat tejaḥ, predicate complement)

sentences.l: The radiance, residing-in-the-sun, that illumines the whole world, and that which [is] in the moon, and that which [is] in fire — know that radiance [to be] mine.
sentences.i: Know that the radiance residing in the sun, which lights up the whole world, and the radiance in the moon and in fire, is mine.
sentences.n: This opens a new section (through verse 15) in which Kṛṣṇa identifies himself with the powers pervading the natural world, beginning with tejaḥ, 'radiance, light': āditya-gatam, 'residing in the sun', it illumines jagat akhilam, 'the whole world', and the same tejaḥ is found candramasi, 'in the moon', and agnau, 'in fire' — recalling 10.21's ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ and closely echoing Kaṭha Upaniṣad 5.15's na tatra sūryo bhāti, na candra-tārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yam agniḥ | tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti — the light of these bodies being itself derivative of the one true light. Sandhi: yadādityagataṃ is yat+āditya-gatam (-t+ā-→-d ā-); tejo is tejaḥ, -aḥ before j-→-o; jagadbhāsayate'khilam packs jagat+bhāsayate (-t+bh-→-d bh-) and bhāsayate+akhilam (-e+a-→-e' with avagraha); yaccandramasi and yaccāgnau both begin yat+ca (-t+c-→-c c-), the second further compounding ca+agnau (a+a→ā); tattejo packs tat+tejaḥ (-t+t-→-t t-, identical stops simply written together) and tejaḥ's own -aḥ before v-→-o.

sentences.t:
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा ।
पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥
sentences.tr:
gām āviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmi aham ojasā |
puṣṇāmi ca oṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somaḥ bhūtvā rasa-ātmakaḥ ||

morph.gloss: the earth (gām: acc. sg. fem., object of āviśya; here in the older sense 'the earth', not 'cow'; simply joined with āviśya, -m unaffected before the vowel)
to enter (āviśya: gerund, 'having entered')
and
a being, a creature (acc. pl. neut., object of dhārayāmi)
to hold, support, sustain (causative; dhārayāmi: present 1st sg., 'I sustain'; dhārayāmi+aham→dhārayāmyaham, -i+a-→-y a-)
I (nom. sg., emphatic subject; simply joined with ojasā, -m unaffected before the vowel)
vigor, vital energy (ojasā: instr. sg., 'by my vigor')
to nourish (puṣṇāmi: present 1st sg., 'I nourish')
and (ca+oṣadhīḥ→cauṣadhīḥ, a+o→au)
a plant, an herb (oṣadhīḥ: acc. pl. fem., object of puṣṇāmi)
all (acc. pl. fem., agreeing with oṣadhīḥ)
Soma, the moon, and the soma-plant/juice of Vedic sacrifice, its senses deliberately overlapping here (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
to become (gerund, 'having become')
sap, essence, flavor (first compound member; rasa+ātmaka→rasātmaka, a+ā→ā)
having the nature of, consisting of (rasa-ātmaka: 'consisting of sap', nom. sg. masc., agreeing with somaḥ)

sentences.l: Having entered the earth, I sustain the creatures by [my] vigor; and I nourish all the plants, having become Soma, consisting of sap.
sentences.i: Having entered the earth, I sustain all creatures by my vigor; and, becoming the sap-giving Soma, I nourish all the plants.
sentences.n: This continues Kṛṣṇa's self-identification with the powers of nature: gām āviśya, 'having entered the earth' (gām here in the older sense 'the earth', not 'a cow'), he dhārayāmi bhūtāni ojasā, 'sustains all beings by [his] vigor' — the same idea of Kṛṣṇa as the hidden support of the physical world as verse 12's tejaḥ in sun, moon and fire; and, becoming somaḥ, 'Soma' (both the moon and the soma-plant/juice central to Vedic sacrifice, its two senses deliberately overlapping here), rasa-ātmakaḥ, 'consisting of sap, essence' (the vital sap that gives plants their nourishing power), he puṣṇāmi oṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ, 'nourishes all the plants' — traditionally read, with Śaṅkara, as an allusion to the moon's influence on plant growth. Sandhi: gāmāviśya is gām+āviśya, simply joined (-m before the vowel unaffected); dhārayāmyaham is dhārayāmi+aham (-i+a-→-y a-); ahamojasā is aham+ojasā, simply joined; cauṣadhīḥ is ca+oṣadhīḥ (a+o→au); somo is somaḥ, -aḥ before bh-→-o; rasātmakaḥ is rasa+ātmaka (a+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः ।
प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥
sentences.tr:
aham vaiśvānaraḥ bhūtvā prāṇinām deham āśritaḥ |
prāṇa-apāna-samāyuktaḥ pacāmi annam catur-vidham ||

morph.gloss: I (nom. sg., subject)
Vaiśvānara, the fire common to all men, the fire of digestion (nom. sg. masc., predicate complement of bhūtvā; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
to become (gerund, 'having become')
a living, breathing being (gen. pl., 'of living beings')
body (deham: acc. sg. masc., object of āśritaḥ; simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
resorted to, dwelling in (āśrita: past participle, āśritaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, agreeing with aham, 'dwelling [in the body]')
the outgoing/upward breath (first compound member; prāṇa+apāna→prāṇāpāna, a+a→ā)
the downward/incoming breath (second member)

sentences.l: I, having become Vaiśvānara, dwelling in the body of living beings, united-with-the-prāṇa-and-apāna-[breaths], digest the fourfold food.
sentences.i: I, becoming Vaiśvānara, the fire of digestion, dwelling in the bodies of living beings and joined with the breaths prāṇa and apāna, digest the four kinds of food.
sentences.n: This continues Kṛṣṇa's identification with nature's powers by turning to digestion: as vaiśvānaraḥ, 'Vaiśvānara' (literally 'belonging to all men', the fire common to every living body, here specifically the digestive fire), he dwells (āśritaḥ) in the deham, 'body', of prāṇinām, 'living beings', and, samāyuktaḥ, 'joined with', the prāṇa and apāna breaths (the upward and downward vital airs of yogic physiology, already invoked at 4.29-30 and 5.27), pacāmi annam catur-vidham, 'digests the fourfold food' — traditionally glossed by Śaṅkara as food that is chewed, sucked, licked and swallowed. Sandhi: vaiśvānaro is vaiśvānaraḥ, -aḥ before bh-→-o; dehamāśritaḥ is deham+āśritaḥ, simply joined; prāṇāpāna- is prāṇa+apāna (a+a→ā); pacāmyannaṃ is pacāmi+annam (-i+a-→-y a-).

मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च ।
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो ।
वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥

sentences.l: And I am seated in the heart of all [beings]; from me [come] memory, knowledge, and its loss; and by all the Vedas, I alone am to be known; and I alone [am] the author of the Vedānta and the knower of the Veda.
sentences.i: I am seated in the hearts of all beings; from me come memory, knowledge, and their loss; and I alone am what is to be known through all the Vedas — I am indeed the author of the Vedānta and the knower of the Veda.
sentences.n: This closes the chapter's central self-revelatory section (verses 12-15) by moving from Kṛṣṇa's presence in nature to his presence within the knowing subject itself: sarvasya hṛdi saṃniviṣṭaḥ, 'seated in the heart of all beings' (echoing 13.17's hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam), he is the source of both smṛtiḥ, 'memory', jñānam, 'knowledge', and apohanam, its own 'removal, forgetting' — extending, to its darker complement (apohana, 'forgetting'), the claim already made of memory's favorable side at 10.34, which names smṛti, 'memory', among Kṛṣṇa's own manifestations. He then declares himself vedyaḥ, 'the one to be known', through the Vedas collectively, and, in a striking pair of titles, both vedānta-kṛt, 'the author of the Vedānta' (the Upaniṣads, the concluding portion of Vedic revelation), and veda-vid, 'the knower of the Veda' — at once the source, the object, and the knower of all sacred learning. Sandhi: cāhaṃ is ca+aham (a+a→ā); saṃniviṣṭo is saṃniviṣṭaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ packs smṛtiḥ+jñānam (-iḥ+j-→-ir j-) and jñānam+apohanam, simply joined; vedaiśca is vedaiḥ+ca (-aiḥ+c-→-aiś c-); sarvairahameva packs sarvaiḥ+aham (-aiḥ+a-→-air a-) and aham+eva, simply joined; vedyo is vedyaḥ, -aḥ before v-→-o; vedāntakṛdvedavideva packs veda+anta (a+a→ā) and vedānta-kṛt+vedavid (-t+v-→-d v-); cāham is ca+aham (a+a→ā).

क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥

kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭasthaḥ akṣaraḥ ucyate ||

the Person (nom. dual masc., subject)
world (loc. sg., 'in the world')
the Perishable, that which flows and decays (kṣaraḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-)
and (ca+akṣaraḥ→cākṣaraḥ, a+a→ā)
the Imperishable — literally 'not-flowing, not-decaying'; the same word also means, unrelatedly, 'a syllable', though not in that sense here (akṣaraḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, second of the pair)

sentences.l: These two Persons [are] in the world: the Perishable, and the Imperishable too. The Perishable [is] all beings; the unchanging [one] is called the Imperishable.
sentences.i: There are two Persons in this world, the Perishable and the Imperishable. The Perishable consists of all beings; the changeless one is called the Imperishable.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's climactic teaching (through verse 19), the doctrine that gives the chapter its name, Puruṣottama-yoga: two puruṣau, 'Persons' (puruṣa, translated 'the Person' throughout this pipeline, as at chapters 8, 10-11 and 13, rather than left untranslated), exist in the world — kṣaraḥ, 'the Perishable' (from kṣar, 'to flow, decay, perish'), identified with sarvāṇi bhūtāni, 'all [finite, changing] beings', and akṣaraḥ, 'the Imperishable' (the plain negation of kṣara; the same word elsewhere, unrelatedly, means 'a syllable', but not here), described as kūṭa-sthaḥ, 'standing on a summit, unmoving, unchanging' — the individual self in its unchanging aspect, as distinct from its ever-changing embodiments. Verses 17-18 go on to name a third, still higher reality beyond both. Sandhi: dvāvimau is dvau+imau (-au+i-→-āv i-); kṣaraścākṣara packs kṣaraḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-) and ca+akṣaraḥ (a+a→ā); akṣara eva shows the visarga of akṣaraḥ dropped before the vowel with the hiatus retained rather than coalescing to ai — an accepted option in epic verse; kūṭastho'kṣara packs kūṭasthaḥ+akṣaraḥ (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha).

sentences.t:
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः ।
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥
sentences.tr:

yaḥ loka-trayam āviśya bibharti avyayaḥ īśvaraḥ ||

sentences.l: But the highest Person [is] another, declared [to be] the Supreme Self — who, having entered the three worlds, sustains [them], the imperishable Lord.
sentences.i: But there is another, the highest Person, called the Supreme Self — the imperishable Lord who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them.
sentences.n: This introduces the third and highest reality, beyond the kṣara-akṣara pair of verse 16: uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ, 'the highest Person', described as parama-ātmā, 'the Supreme Self' (a title used elsewhere of the innermost reality present in every being, e.g. 6.7, 13.22), and as avyayaḥ īśvaraḥ, 'the imperishable Lord' who, loka-trayam āviśya, 'having pervaded the three worlds' (earth, atmosphere and heaven), bibharti, 'sustains, upholds' them — anticipating the direct self-identification with this uttama-puruṣa that Kṛṣṇa makes in verses 18-19. Sandhi: puruṣastvanyaḥ packs puruṣaḥ+tu (-aḥ+t-→-as t-) and tu+anyaḥ (-u+a-→-v a-, yaṇ); paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ packs parama+ātmā (a+ā→ā), ātmā+iti (ā+i→e), and iti+udāhṛtaḥ (-i+u-→-y u-); lokatrayamāviśya is loka-trayam+āviśya, simply joined; bibhartyavyaya is bibharti+avyayaḥ (-i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t:
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः ।
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥

yasmāt kṣaram atītaḥ aham akṣarāt api ca uttamaḥ |
ataḥ asmi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣa-uttamaḥ ||

highest (puruṣa-uttama: 'the Supreme Person', nom. sg. masc., in apposition with the subject; the title that gives this chapter its name, rendered 'Supreme Person' wherever the compound occurs. Arjuna has already used it as a vocative at 8.1, 10.15 and 11.3, where it may be only an honorific, 'best of men'; here Kṛṣṇa defines it as his own: the Person beyond the Perishable and the Imperishable)

sentences.l: Since I am beyond the Perishable, and superior even to the Imperishable — therefore, in the world and in the Veda, I am celebrated [as] the Supreme Person.
sentences.i: Because I transcend the Perishable, and am higher even than the Imperishable, I am therefore celebrated, in the world and in the Veda, as the Supreme Person.
sentences.n: This is the chapter's title verse, Kṛṣṇa's own naming of himself as puruṣottamaḥ, 'the Supreme Person' (puruṣa uttama, 'highest of persons' — the very compound already used as a vocative address to Kṛṣṇa at 8.1, 10.15 and 11.3, now Kṛṣṇa's own declared identity, and the term that gives this chapter, Puruṣottama-yoga, its name): he stands beyond even the pairing of verses 16-17, atītaḥ kṣaram, 'transcending the Perishable' (the changing multiplicity of embodied beings), and uttamaḥ akṣarāt api, 'higher even than the Imperishable' (the unchanging individual self) — a third and highest term beyond both, prathitaḥ loke vede ca, 'renowned in the world and in the Veda'. Sandhi: yasmātkṣaram is yasmāt+kṣaram, simply joined (no change before k-); atīto'ham is atītaḥ+aham (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); akṣarādapi is akṣarāt+api (-t+a-→-d a-, voicing before a vowel); cottamaḥ is ca+uttamaḥ (a+u→o); ato'smi is ataḥ+asmi (-aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); puruṣottamaḥ is puruṣa+uttama (a+u→o).

यो मामेवमसंमूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥

sa sarva-vit bhajati mām sarva-bhāvena bhārata ||

to know (jānāti: present 3rd sg., 'knows')
the Person (first compound member; puruṣa+uttamam→puruṣottamam, a+u→o)

sentences.l: Who, thus undeluded, knows me [as] the Supreme Person — he, all-knowing, worships me with his whole being, O Bhārata.
sentences.i: Whoever, undeluded in this way, knows me as the Supreme Person, knows all there is to know, and worships me with his whole being, Bhārata.
sentences.n: This closes the puruṣottama teaching with its practical fruit: whoever mām evam asaṃmūḍhaḥ jānāti puruṣottamam, 'thus undeluded knows me as the Supreme Person' just declared in verse 18, becomes sa sarva-vit, 'a knower of all' (knowing the highest, he implicitly knows all that is derived from it, as at 7.2's yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo'nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate), and bhajati mām sarva-bhāvena, 'worships me with his whole being' — undivided devotion again named as the fruit of the highest knowledge, as at 7.19's vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā su-durlabhaḥ. Sandhi: māmevamasaṃmūḍho packs mām+evam (simply joined) and evam+asaṃmūḍhaḥ (simply joined), whose own -aḥ before j-→-o; puruṣottamam is puruṣa+uttamam (a+u→o); sarvavidbhajati is sarva-vit+bhajati (-t+bh-→-d bh-).

इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ ।
एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥

etat buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛta-kṛtyaḥ ca bhārata ||

and
descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: Thus this most-secret teaching has been declared by me, O blameless one. Having understood this, one would become wise, and one who has accomplished his purpose, O Bhārata.
sentences.i: Thus have I declared this most secret teaching, blameless one. Understanding this, a person becomes wise, Bhārata, and has accomplished all that needs to be done.
sentences.n: This closes the chapter with a formal envoi typical of the Gītā's chapter-endings: iti guhyatamam śāstram, 'this most secret teaching' (guhyatama, superlative of guhya, 'secret', marking the puruṣottama doctrine of verses 16-19 as among the poem's innermost teachings, echoing 9.1's guhyatamam and anticipating 18.63's guhyād guhyataram and 18.64's sarva-guhyatamam), has been uktam mayā, 'declared by me'; whoever etat buddhvā, 'having understood this', becomes buddhimān, 'wise, intelligent', and kṛta-kṛtyaḥ, 'one who has accomplished what was to be accomplished' (a set phrase for having fulfilled the whole purpose of life), closing the chapter on the promise already made, in different terms, at verse 19's fruit of undivided devotion. Sandhi: śāstramidamuktaṃ is śāstram+idam and idam+uktam, both simply joined (-m unaffected before the vowels i- and u-); mayānagha is mayā+anagha (ā+a→ā); etadbuddhvā is etat+buddhvā (-t+b-→-d b-); buddhimānsyāt is buddhimān+syāt, simply joined; kṛtakṛtyaśca is kṛtakṛtyaḥ+ca (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-).

glossary.यस्तं: yaḥ tam — yad — who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative, subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-); tad — it, him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of veda, referring to the tree)

glossary.स: sa — tad — he (sa: nom. sg. masc., subject, correlative)
glossary.वेदवित्: veda-vit — veda — the Veda (first compound member); vid — knowing, a knower (agent noun from vid; veda-vit: 'a knower of the Veda', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.अधश्चोर्ध्वं: adhaḥ ca ūrdhvam — adhas — below, downward (adhaḥ: adverb; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-); ca — and (ca+ūrdhvam→cordhvam, a+ū→o); ūrdhva — above, upward (ūrdhvam: adverb)
glossary.प्रसृतास्तस्य: prasṛtāḥ tasya — pra-sṛ — spread forth, extended (prasṛta: past participle, nom. pl. fem., predicate, agreeing with śākhāḥ; -āḥ+t-→-ās t-); tad — its (tasya: gen. sg., referring to the tree of verse 1)
glossary.शाखा: śākhāḥ — śākhā — branch (nom. pl. fem., subject; the visarga of -āḥ is silently elided before the following voiced g- of guṇapravṛddhāḥ, carried across the pāda break — a pattern distinct from the more familiar -aḥ→-o, and recurring wherever a plural in -āḥ meets a voiced sound)
glossary.गुणप्रवृद्धा: guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ — guṇa — quality; the guṇas, kept untranslated in the idiomatic rendering per convention (first compound member); pra-vṛdh — grown, increased (pravṛddha: past participle, guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ: 'nourished/increased by the guṇas', nom. pl. fem., agreeing with śākhāḥ; its own -āḥ likewise elides before the voiced v- of viṣaya- that follows)
glossary.विषयप्रवालाः: viṣaya-pravālāḥ — viṣaya — a sense-object, an object of the senses (first compound member); pravāla — sprout, new shoot, tender twig (viṣaya-pravālāḥ: 'having sense-objects as their new shoots', nom. pl. fem., agreeing with śākhāḥ)
glossary.अधश्च: adhaḥ ca — adhas — below, downward (adhaḥ: adverb; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-); ca — and
glossary.मूलान्यनुसंततानि: mūlāni anusaṃtatāni — mūla — root (mūlāni: nom. pl. neut., subject; -i+a-→-y a-); anu-saṃ-tan — stretched out, extended continuously (anusaṃtata: past participle, nom. pl. neut., predicate, agreeing with mūlāni)
glossary.कर्मानुबन्धीनि: karma-anubandhīni — karman — action (first compound member; karma+anubandhīni→karmānubandhīni, a+a→ā); anu-bandhin — binding to, entailing (from anu-bandh, 'to bind, entail consequences'; karma-anubandhīni: 'bound to action, entailing the consequences of action', nom. pl. neut., agreeing with mūlāni)
glossary.मनुष्यलोके: manuṣya-loke — manuṣya — man, human being (first compound member); loka — world (manuṣya-loka: 'the human world', loc. sg.)
glossary.रूपमस्येह: rūpam asya iha — rūpa — form, shape (rūpam: nom. sg. neut., subject; simply joined with asya, -m unaffected before the vowel); tad — its (asya: gen. sg., referring to the tree); iha — here, in this world (asya+iha→asyeha, a+i→e)
glossary.तथोपलभ्यते: tathā upalabhyate — tathā — thus, in that way (adverb; tathā+upalabhyate→tathopalabhyate, ā+u→o); upa-labh — to perceive, apprehend (upalabhyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is apprehended')
glossary.नान्तो: na antaḥ — na — not (na+antaḥ→nāntaḥ, a+a→ā); anta — end (antaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
glossary.चादिर्न: ca ādiḥ na — ca — and (ca+ādiḥ→cādiḥ, a+ā→ā); ādi — beginning (ādiḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -iḥ+n-→-ir n-); na — not, nor (repeated)
glossary.संप्रतिष्ठा: saṃpratiṣṭhā — sam-prati-sthā — foundation, resting-place, stable basis (nom. sg. fem., subject)
glossary.अश्वत्थमेनं: aśvattham enam — aśvattha — the aśvattha tree (acc. sg. masc., object of chittvā, resuming the tree of verses 1-2); etad — this (enam: acc. sg. masc., emphatic, agreeing with aśvattham; simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel)
glossary.सुविरूढमूल-: su-virūḍha-mūla(m)- — su — well, thoroughly (prefix, first member); vi-ruh — grown up, sprung up (virūḍha: past participle, second member, 'well-grown'); mūla — root (third member; su-virūḍha-mūlam: 'having well-grown roots', bahuvrīhi, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with aśvattham enam — uniquely in this chapter the word's final -m is carried, by ordinary sandhi with the following vowel, onto the far side of the pāda break; this is an authentic feature of the transmitted text, reproduced here exactly as given and not a misprint — see the note)
glossary.मसङ्गशस्त्रेण: (-m) asaṅga-śastreṇa — mūla — root (this token opens with the -m that completes the previous line's mūlam, fused by sandhi with the following vowel and carried across the line break; -m+a-→ simply joined); a-saṅga — non-attachment, freedom from attachment (first compound member of this word); śastra — a weapon, a blade (asaṅga-śastra: 'the weapon of non-attachment', instr. sg.)
glossary.दृढेन: dṛḍhena — dṛḍha — firm, strong (instr. sg. neut., agreeing with śastreṇa)
glossary.छित्त्वा: chittvā — chid — to cut, sever (chittvā: gerund, 'having cut down')
glossary.ततः: tataḥ — tatas — from that, then, thence (adverb)
glossary.पदं: padam — pada — place, state, station (nom. sg. neut., subject of the passive gerundive parimārgitavyam)
glossary.तत्परिमार्गितव्यं: tat parimārgitavyam — tad — that (tat: nom. sg. neut., in apposition with padam, 'that [state]'); pari-mārg — to seek out, track down (parimārgitavya: gerundive, 'is to be sought out', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with padam)
glossary.यस्मिन्गता: yasmin gatāḥ — yad — which (yasmin: loc. sg. neut. relative, 'into which, wherein'); gam — to go (gata: past participle, gatāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, 'having gone [there]'; simply written joined, the nasal of yasmin unaffected before the consonant g-)
glossary.निवर्तन्ति: nivartanti — ni-vṛt — to turn back, return (nivartanti: present 3rd pl., 'they return')
glossary.तमेव: tam eva — tad — that, him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of prapadye, referring forward to puruṣam); eva — indeed, alone
glossary.चाद्यं: ca ādyam — ca — and (ca+ādyam→cādyam, a+ā→ā); ādya — primal, original, first (ādyam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣam)
glossary.पुरुषं: puruṣam — puruṣa — the Person (acc. sg. masc., object of prapadye)
glossary.प्रपद्ये: prapadye — pra-pad — to take refuge in, resort to (prapadye: present middle 1st sg., 'I take refuge in')
glossary.यतः: yataḥ — yatas — from whom, from which (adverb/relative, referring to puruṣam)
glossary.प्रवृत्तिः: pravṛttiḥ — pra-vṛt — activity, outgoing tendency, active engagement (nom. sg. fem., subject)
glossary.प्रसृता: prasṛtā — pra-sṛ — spread forth, issued forth (prasṛtā: past participle, nom. sg. fem., predicate, agreeing with pravṛttiḥ)
glossary.पुराणी: purāṇī — purāṇa — ancient, primeval (purāṇī: nom. sg. fem., agreeing with pravṛttiḥ)
glossary.निर्मानमोहा: nirmāna-mohāḥ — nir-māna — free from pride, without self-conceit (nirmāna: first member of the bahuvrīhi); moha — delusion (nirmāna-moha: 'free from pride and delusion', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject; the visarga of the plural -āḥ is elided before the following voiced j- of jitasaṅgadoṣāḥ, as at verse 2's śākhā and guṇapravṛddhā)
glossary.जितसङ्गदोषा: jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ — ji — conquered, overcome (jita: past participle, first member); saṅga — attachment (second member); doṣa — fault, flaw (jita-saṅga-doṣa: 'having conquered the fault of attachment', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc.; its own -āḥ elides before the following voiced a- of adhyātmanityāḥ)
glossary.अध्यात्मनित्या: adhyātma-nityāḥ — adhi-ātman — pertaining to the self, the inner self (adhyātma: first compound member, adhi+ātman→adhyātma, the same term named at 8.3); nitya — constant, ever intent on (adhyātma-nitya: 'ever intent on the inner self', nom. pl. masc.; its -āḥ elides before the voiced v- of vinivṛttakāmāḥ)
glossary.विनिवृत्तकामाः: vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ — vi-ni-vṛt — turned back, ceased, withdrawn (vinivṛtta: past participle, first member); kāma — desire (vinivṛtta-kāma: 'whose desires have ceased', bahuvrīhi, nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः: dvandvaiḥ vimuktāḥ — dvandva — a pair of opposites, a duality (dvandvaiḥ: instr. pl., 'by/from the dualities'); vi-muc — freed, released (vimukta: past participle, vimuktāḥ: nom. pl. masc., 'freed'; -aiḥ+v-→-air v-)
glossary.सुखदुःखसंज्ञै-: sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñaiḥ- — sukha — happiness, pleasure (first compound member); duḥkha — pain, suffering (second member); saṃjñā — name, designation (sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñā: 'called/designated pleasure and pain', instr. pl., in apposition with dvandvaiḥ — as at verse 3, the source splits this compound exactly at the point where its final visarga fuses by sandhi with the following gacchanti, carrying an 'r' onto the next printed line; reproduced here as given, not a misprint — see the note)
glossary.र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः: (-r) gacchanti amūḍhāḥ — gam — to go (gacchanti: present 3rd pl., 'they go'; its initial r completes the sandhi of saṃjñaiḥ from the previous line, -aiḥ+g-→-air g-; gacchanti+amūḍhāḥ→gacchantyamūḍhāḥ, -i+a-→-y a-); a-mūḍha — undeluded, unconfused (amūḍhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject, in apposition with all the preceding predicate adjectives)
glossary.पदमव्ययं: padam avyayam — pada — place, state (acc. sg. neut., object of gacchanti); a-vyaya — imperishable (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with padam)
glossary.तत्: tat — tad — that (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with padam, resuming verse 4's tat parimārgitavyam)
glossary.तद्भासयते: tat bhāsayate — tad — that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of bhāsayate, referring to the padam of verse 5; -t+bh-→-d bh-); bhās — to illumine, shine upon (causative; bhāsayate: present middle 3rd sg. used in an active sense, 'illumines')
glossary.सूर्यो: sūryaḥ — sūrya — the sun (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
glossary.शशाङ्को: śaśāṅkaḥ — śaśa — hare (first compound member); aṅka — mark, spot (śaśa-aṅka: 'the hare-marked one', i.e. the moon, nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before n-→-o)
glossary.पावकः: pāvakaḥ — pāvaka — fire (nom. sg. masc., subject)
glossary.यद्गत्वा: yat gatvā — yad — which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object of gatvā, referring to the imperishable state; -t+g-→-d g-); gam — to go (gatvā: gerund, 'having gone [to which]')
glossary.निवर्तन्ते: nivartante — ni-vṛt — to return (nivartante: present middle 3rd pl., 'they return')
glossary.तद्धाम: tat dhāma — tad — that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; -t+dh-→-d dh-); dhāman — abode, seat, glory (dhāma: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.परमं: paramam — parama — highest, supreme (paramam: nom. sg. neut., agreeing with dhāma)
glossary.ममैवांशो: mama eva aṃśaḥ — aham — I (mama: gen. sg. 'my'); eva — indeed (mama+eva→mamaiva, a+e→ai); aṃśa — a part, a portion, a fragment (aṃśaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before j-→-o)
glossary.जीवलोके: jīva-loke — jīva — a living being, a soul (first compound member); loka — world (jīva-loka: 'the world of living beings', loc. sg.)
glossary.जीवभूतः: jīva-bhūtaḥ — jīva — living, life (first compound member); bhū — become (bhūta: past participle, jīva-bhūta: 'become a living being, a jīva', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.सनातनः: sanātanaḥ — sanātana — eternal, everlasting (nom. sg. masc., agreeing with aṃśaḥ)
glossary.मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि: manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi — manas — mind (first compound member; visarga retained before ṣ-, as at verse 1's adhaḥśākham); ṣaṣṭha — sixth (manaḥ-ṣaṣṭha: 'with the mind as sixth', bahuvrīhi describing indriyāṇi; manaḥṣaṣṭhāni+indriyāṇi→manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi, -i+i-→-ī-, vowel lengthening); indriya — a sense-organ, a faculty (indriyāṇi: acc. pl. neut., object of karṣati)
glossary.प्रकृतिस्थानि: prakṛti-sthāni — prakṛti — nature (first compound member); stha — abiding in, situated in (prakṛti-sthāni: 'seated in nature', acc. pl. neut., agreeing with indriyāṇi)
glossary.कर्षति: karṣati — kṛṣ — to draw, drag (karṣati: present 3rd sg., 'draws [to itself]')
glossary.शरीरं: śarīram — śarīra — body (acc. sg. neut., object of avāpnoti)
glossary.यदवाप्नोति: yat avāpnoti — yad — which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object, referring to śarīram; -t+a-→-d a-, a final stop voiced before a vowel); ava-āp — to obtain, acquire (avāpnoti: present 3rd sg., 'obtains')
glossary.यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः: yat ca api utkrāmati īśvaraḥ — yad — which, and (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, further object with ca; -t+c-→-c c-); ca — and; api — also, even (ca+api→cāpi, a+a→ā); ud-kram — to go forth, depart (utkrāmati: present 3rd sg., 'departs'; api+utkrāmati→cāpyutkrāmati, -i+u-→-y u-); īśvara — the lord, the ruling one — here the individual soul as controller of its own body and senses (nom. sg. masc., subject; utkrāmati+īśvaraḥ→utkrāmatīśvaraḥ, -i+ī-→-ī-)
glossary.गृहीत्वैतानि: gṛhītvā etāni — grah — to seize, take hold of (gṛhītvā: gerund, 'having taken hold of'); etad — these (etāni: acc. pl. neut., object of gṛhītvā, referring to the senses of verse 7; gṛhītvā+etāni→gṛhītvaitāni, ā+e→ai)
glossary.संयाति: saṃyāti — sam-yā — to go along with, proceed (saṃyāti: present 3rd sg., 'proceeds')
glossary.वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात्: vāyuḥ gandhān iva āśayāt — vāyu — wind, air (vāyuḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject of the simile; -uḥ+g-→-ur g-); gandha — scent, odor (gandhān: acc. pl. masc., understood object of an implied verb of carrying, completing the simile; simply joined with iva); iva — like, as (particle of comparison); āśaya — a receptacle, a resting-place (e.g. a flower) (āśayāt: abl. sg., 'from [its] resting-place'; iva+āśayāt→ivāśayāt, a+ā→ā)
glossary.श्रोत्रं: śrotram — śrotra — the ear, hearing (acc. sg. neut., object of adhiṣṭhāya)
glossary.चक्षुः: cakṣuḥ — cakṣus — the eye, sight (acc. sg. neut., object)
glossary.स्पर्शनं: sparśanam — sparśana — touch, the sense of touch (acc. sg. neut., object)
glossary.रसनं: rasanam — rasana — taste, the sense of taste (acc. sg. neut., object)
glossary.घ्राणमेव: ghrāṇam eva — ghrāṇa — smell, the sense of smell (acc. sg. neut., object; simply joined with eva, -m unaffected before the vowel); eva — indeed, too
glossary.अधिष्ठाय: adhiṣṭhāya — adhi-sthā — to preside over, take control of (adhiṣṭhāya: gerund, 'having taken control of')
glossary.मनश्चायं: manaḥ ca ayam — manas — the mind (manaḥ: acc. sg. neut., additional object of adhiṣṭhāya; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-); ca — and; idam — this (ayam: nom. sg. masc., subject, referring to the soul; ca+ayam→cāyam, a+a→ā)
glossary.विषयानुपसेवते: viṣayān upasevate — viṣaya — a sense-object (viṣayān: acc. pl. masc., object of upasevate); upa-sev — to resort to, enjoy, partake of (upasevate: present middle 3rd sg., 'partakes of')
glossary.उत्क्रामन्तं: utkrāmantam — ud-kram — departing, going forth (utkrāmant: present participle, utkrāmantam: acc. sg. masc., object of anupaśyanti/paśyanti, referring to the soul)
glossary.स्थितं: sthitam — sthā — abiding, remaining (sthita: past participle, acc. sg. masc., 'remaining [in the body]')
glossary.वापि: vā api — vā — or (vā+api→vāpi, ā+a→ā); api — also, even (emphatic)
glossary.भुञ्जानं: bhuñjānam — bhuj — enjoying, partaking of (bhuñjāna: present middle participle, acc. sg. masc., 'enjoying [the sense-objects]')
glossary.गुणान्वितम्: guṇa-anvitam — guṇa — the guṇas, kept untranslated per convention (first compound member; guṇa+anvitam→guṇānvitam, a+a→ā); anvita — accompanied by, united with (from anu-i; guṇa-anvita: 'united with the guṇas', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with the soul)
glossary.विमूढा: vimūḍhāḥ — vi-muh — deluded, confused (vimūḍha: past participle, vimūḍhāḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; the visarga elides before the following voiced n- of na, as at verse 2's śākhā and verse 5's nirmānamohāḥ)
glossary.नानुपश्यन्ति: na anupaśyanti — na — not; anu-dṛś — to perceive, see (anupaśyanti: present 3rd pl., 'they perceive'; na+anupaśyanti→nānupaśyanti, a+a→ā)
glossary.पश्यन्ति: paśyanti — dṛś — to see (paśyanti: present 3rd pl., 'they see')
glossary.ज्ञानचक्षुषः: jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ — jñāna — knowledge (first compound member); cakṣus — eye (jñāna-cakṣus: 'those whose eye is knowledge, those possessing the eye of knowledge', nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.यतन्तो: yatantaḥ — yat — to strive, make effort (yatant: present participle, yatantaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ before y-→-o)
glossary.योगिनश्चैनं: yoginaḥ ca enam — yogin — a yogin (yoginaḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition with yatantaḥ; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-); ca — and; etad — this, it (enam: acc. sg. masc., object of paśyanti, referring to the self; ca+enam→cainam, a+e→ai)
glossary.पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम्: paśyanti ātmani avasthitam — dṛś — to see (paśyanti: present 3rd pl.; paśyanti+ātmani→paśyantyātmani, -i+ā-→-y ā-); ātman — the self (ātmani: loc. sg., 'in the self'); ava-sthā — abiding, situated (avasthita: past participle, acc. sg. masc., agreeing with enam; ātmani+avasthitam→ātmanyavasthitam, -i+a-→-y a-)
glossary.यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो: yatantaḥ api akṛta-ātmānaḥ — yat — to strive, make effort (yatant: present participle, yatantaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); api — even, also (api+akṛtātmānaḥ→apyakṛtātmānaḥ, -i+a-→-y a-); a-kṛta-ātman — one whose self is unaccomplished, unperfected (bahuvrīhi; akṛtātmānaḥ: nom. pl. masc., in apposition with yatantaḥ; -aḥ before n-→-o)
glossary.नैनं: na enam — na — not (na+enam→nainam, a+e→ai); etad — him, it (enam: acc. sg. masc., object of paśyanti)
glossary.पश्यन्त्यचेतसः: paśyanti acetasaḥ — dṛś — to see (paśyanti: present 3rd pl.; paśyanti+acetasaḥ→paśyantyacetasaḥ, -i+a-→-y a-); a-cetas — unintelligent, lacking discernment (acetasaḥ: nom. pl. masc., subject)
glossary.यदादित्यगतं: yat āditya-gatam — yad — which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, subject; yat+āditya→yadāditya, -t+ā-→-d ā-); āditya — the sun (first compound member); gam — to go (gata: past participle, 'residing in' — āditya-gata: 'residing in the sun', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with tejaḥ)
glossary.तेजो: tejaḥ — tejas — light, radiance, splendor (nom. sg. neut., subject; -aḥ before j-→-o)
glossary.जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम्: jagat bhāsayate akhilam — jagat — the world (acc. sg. neut., object of bhāsayate; jagat+bhāsayate→jagadbhāsayate, -t+bh-→-d bh-); bhās — to illumine (causative; bhāsayate: present middle 3rd sg. used actively, 'illumines'); a-khila — whole, entire (akhilam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat; bhāsayate+akhilam→bhāsayate'khilam, -e+a-→-e' with avagraha)
glossary.यच्चन्द्रमसि: yat ca candramasi — yad — which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, continuing the subject; -t+c-→-c c-); ca — and; candramas — the moon (candramasi: loc. sg., 'in the moon')
glossary.यच्चाग्नौ: yat ca agnau — yad — which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative; -t+c-→-c c-); ca — and (ca+agnau→cāgnau, a+a→ā); agni — fire (agnau: loc. sg., 'in fire')
glossary.तत्तेजो: tat tejaḥ — tad — that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of viddhi; -t+t-→-t t-); tejas — radiance, light (tejaḥ: acc. sg. neut., in apposition with tat; -aḥ before v-→-o)
glossary.विद्धि: viddhi — vid — to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg., 'know!')
glossary.मामकम्: māmakam — māmaka — mine, belonging to me (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with tat tejaḥ, predicate complement)

glossary.भूतानि: bhūtāni — bhūta — a being, a creature (acc. pl. neut., object of dhārayāmi)
glossary.धारयाम्यहमोजसा: dhārayāmi aham ojasā — dhṛ — to hold, support, sustain (causative; dhārayāmi: present 1st sg., 'I sustain'; dhārayāmi+aham→dhārayāmyaham, -i+a-→-y a-); aham — I (nom. sg., emphatic subject; simply joined with ojasā, -m unaffected before the vowel); ojas — vigor, vital energy (ojasā: instr. sg., 'by my vigor')
glossary.पुष्णामि: puṣṇāmi — puṣ — to nourish (puṣṇāmi: present 1st sg., 'I nourish')
glossary.चौषधीः: ca oṣadhīḥ — ca — and (ca+oṣadhīḥ→cauṣadhīḥ, a+o→au); oṣadhi — a plant, an herb (oṣadhīḥ: acc. pl. fem., object of puṣṇāmi)

glossary.सोमो: somaḥ — soma — Soma, the moon, and the soma-plant/juice of Vedic sacrifice, its senses deliberately overlapping here (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
