glossary.वैश्वानरो: vaiśvānaraḥ — vaiśvānara — Vaiśvānara, the fire common to all men, the fire of digestion (nom. sg. masc., predicate complement of bhūtvā; -aḥ before bh-→-o)
glossary.प्राणिनां: prāṇinām — prāṇin — a living, breathing being (gen. pl., 'of living beings')
glossary.देहमाश्रितः: deham āśritaḥ — deha — body (deham: acc. sg. masc., object of āśritaḥ; simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel); ā-śri — resorted to, dwelling in (āśrita: past participle, āśritaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, agreeing with aham, 'dwelling [in the body]')
glossary.प्राणापानसमायुक्तः: prāṇa-apāna-samāyuktaḥ — prāṇa — the outgoing/upward breath (first compound member; prāṇa+apāna→prāṇāpāna, a+a→ā); apāna — the downward/incoming breath (second member); sam-ā-yuj — joined together with, united with (samāyukta: past participle, nom. sg. masc., agreeing with aham, 'united with the prāṇa and apāna breaths')
glossary.पचाम्यन्नं: pacāmi annam — pac — to cook, digest (pacāmi: present 1st sg., 'I digest'; pacāmi+annam→pacāmyannam, -i+a-→-y a-); anna — food (acc. sg. neut., object of pacāmi)
glossary.चतुर्विधम्: catur-vidham — catur — four (first compound member); vidha — kind, sort (catur-vidha: 'fourfold', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with annam)
glossary.चाहं: ca aham — ca — and (ca+aham→cāham, a+a→ā); aham — I (nom. sg., subject)
glossary.हृदि: hṛdi — hṛd — heart (loc. sg., 'in the heart')
glossary.संनिविष्टो: saṃniviṣṭaḥ — sam-ni-viś — entered, seated, established (saṃniviṣṭa: past participle, nom. sg. masc., predicate, agreeing with aham; -aḥ before m-→-o)
glossary.मत्तः: mattaḥ — mad — from me (mattaḥ: abl. sg. of aham)
glossary.स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं: smṛtiḥ jñānam apohanam — smṛti — memory (smṛtiḥ: nom. sg. fem., subject; -iḥ+j-→-ir j-); jñāna — knowledge (jñānam: nom. sg. neut., subject, additional item; simply joined with apohanam, -m unaffected before the vowel); apa-ūh — removal, taking away, forgetting (apohana: nom. sg. neut., subject, 'the loss [of knowledge]')
glossary.वेदैश्च: vedaiḥ ca — veda — the Veda (vedaiḥ: instr. pl., 'by/through the Vedas'; -aiḥ+c-→-aiś c-); ca — and
glossary.सर्वैरहमेव: sarvaiḥ aham eva — sarva — all (sarvaiḥ: instr. pl., agreeing with vedaiḥ; -aiḥ+a-→-air a-); aham — I (nom. sg., subject; simply joined with eva, -m unaffected before the vowel); eva — indeed, alone
glossary.वेद्यो: vedyaḥ — vid — to be known (gerundive: vedya, 'to be known'; vedyaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before v-→-o)
glossary.वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव: veda-anta-kṛt veda-vid eva — veda — the Veda (first compound member; veda+anta→vedānta, a+a→ā); anta — end (veda-anta: 'the end of the Veda', i.e. the Upaniṣads); kṛt — maker, author (veda-anta-kṛt: 'the author of the Vedānta', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -t+v-→-d v-); veda — the Veda (second compound, first member); vid — a knower (veda-vid: 'the knower of the Veda', nom. sg. masc., predicate; simply joined with eva)
glossary.चाहम्: ca aham — ca — and (ca+aham→cāham, a+a→ā); aham — I (nom. sg., subject, resumptive)
glossary.द्वाविमौ: dvau imau — dvi — two (dvau: nom. dual masc.; dvau+imau→dvāvimau, -au+i-→-āv i-); idam — these (imau: nom. dual masc., agreeing with puruṣau)
glossary.पुरुषौ: puruṣau — puruṣa — the Person (nom. dual masc., subject)
glossary.लोके: loke — loka — world (loc. sg., 'in the world')
glossary.क्षरश्चाक्षर: kṣaraḥ ca akṣaraḥ — kṣara — the Perishable, that which flows and decays (kṣaraḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-); ca — and (ca+akṣaraḥ→cākṣaraḥ, a+a→ā); a-kṣara — the Imperishable — literally 'not-flowing, not-decaying'; the same word also means, unrelatedly, 'a syllable', though not in that sense here (akṣaraḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, second of the pair)
glossary.एव: eva — eva — indeed, too (akṣaraḥ+eva: the visarga of akṣaraḥ drops before the vowel with the hiatus retained rather than coalescing to -ai-, an accepted option in epic verse)
glossary.क्षरः: kṣaraḥ — kṣara — the Perishable (nom. sg. masc., subject, defining the first of the two Persons)
glossary.सर्वाणि: sarvāṇi — sarva — all (nom. pl. neut., agreeing with bhūtāni)
glossary.कूटस्थोऽक्षर: kūṭasthaḥ akṣaraḥ — kūṭa-stha — standing on a summit; unmoving, immutable (kūṭastha: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); a-kṣara — the Imperishable (nom. sg. masc., predicate, 'is called')
glossary.उच्यते: ucyate — vac — to say, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg., 'is called')
glossary.उत्तमः: uttamaḥ — uttama — highest, supreme (nom. sg. masc., agreeing with puruṣaḥ)
glossary.पुरुषस्त्वन्यः: puruṣaḥ tu anyaḥ — puruṣa — the Person (nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ+t-→-as t-); tu — but (tu+anyaḥ→tvanyaḥ, -u+a-→-v a-, yaṇ sandhi); anya — other, different (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः: parama-ātmā iti udāhṛtaḥ — parama — highest, supreme (first compound member; parama+ātmā→paramātmā, a+ā→ā); ātman — self (paramātmā: nom. sg. masc., predicate; ātmā+iti→ātmeti, ā+i→e); iti — thus, [called] (quotation particle; iti+udāhṛtaḥ→ityudāhṛtaḥ, -i+u-→-y u-); ud-ā-hṛ — declared, proclaimed (udāhṛta: past participle, nom. sg. masc., predicate, agreeing with puruṣaḥ)
glossary.यो: yaḥ — yad — who (nom. sg. masc. relative, subject)
glossary.लोकत्रयमाविश्य: loka-trayam āviśya — loka — world (first compound member); traya — a set of three (loka-traya: 'the three worlds', acc. sg. neut., object of āviśya; simply joined, -m unaffected before the vowel); ā-viś — to enter, pervade (āviśya: gerund, 'having entered')
glossary.बिभर्त्यव्यय: bibharti avyayaḥ — bhṛ — to support, sustain, uphold (bibharti: present 3rd sg., 'sustains'; bibharti+avyayaḥ→bibhartyavyayaḥ, -i+a-→-y a-); a-vyaya — imperishable, undecaying (avyayaḥ: nom. sg. masc., agreeing with īśvaraḥ)
glossary.ईश्वरः: īśvaraḥ — īśvara — lord, ruler (nom. sg. masc., in apposition with yaḥ)
glossary.यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि: yasmāt kṣaram atītaḥ aham akṣarāt api — yad — since, because (yasmāt: abl. sg. neut. used as conjunction; simply joined with kṣaram); kṣara — the Perishable (kṣaram: acc. sg., object of atītaḥ, 'transcended beyond the Perishable'); ati-i — transcended, gone beyond (atīta: past participle, atītaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, agreeing with aham; -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); aham — I (nom. sg., subject); a-kṣara — the Imperishable (akṣarāt: abl. sg., 'than the Imperishable'; akṣarāt+api→akṣarādapi, -t+a-→-d a-); api — even, also
glossary.चोत्तमः: ca uttamaḥ — ca — and (ca+uttamaḥ→cottamaḥ, a+u→o); uttama — highest, superior (uttamaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, agreeing with aham)
glossary.अतोऽस्मि: ataḥ asmi — atas — therefore, hence (ataḥ+asmi→ato'smi, -aḥ+a-→-o' with avagraha); as — to be (asmi: present 1st sg., 'I am')
glossary.प्रथितः: prathitaḥ — prath — spread abroad, renowned, celebrated (prathita: past participle, nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.पुरुषोत्तमः: puruṣa-uttamaḥ — puruṣa — the Person (first compound member; puruṣa+uttamaḥ→puruṣottamaḥ, a+u→o); uttama — highest (puruṣa-uttama: 'the Supreme Person', nom. sg. masc., in apposition with the subject; the title that gives this chapter its name, rendered 'Supreme Person' wherever the compound occurs. Arjuna has already used it as a vocative at 8.1, 10.15 and 11.3, where it may be only an honorific, 'best of men'; here Kṛṣṇa defines it as his own: the Person beyond the Perishable and the Imperishable)
glossary.मामेवमसंमूढो: mām evam asaṃmūḍhaḥ — aham — me (mām: acc. sg., object of jānāti; simply joined with evam, -m unaffected before the vowel); evam — thus, in this way (adverb; simply joined with asaṃmūḍhaḥ); a-saṃmūḍha — undeluded, unconfused (asaṃmūḍhaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject, agreeing with yaḥ; -aḥ before j-→-o)
glossary.जानाति: jānāti — jñā — to know (jānāti: present 3rd sg., 'knows')
glossary.पुरुषोत्तमम्: puruṣa-uttamam — puruṣa — the Person (first compound member; puruṣa+uttamam→puruṣottamam, a+u→o); uttama — highest (puruṣa-uttamam: 'the Supreme Person', acc. sg. masc., object of jānāti)
glossary.सर्वविद्भजति: sarva-vit bhajati — sarva — all (first compound member); vid — knowing (sarva-vit: 'knower of all, all-knowing', nom. sg. masc., in apposition with sa; vit+bhajati→vidbhajati, -t+bh-→-d bh-); bhaj — to worship, revere, serve (bhajati: present 3rd sg., 'worships')
glossary.मां: mām — aham — me (acc. sg., object of bhajati)
glossary.सर्वभावेन: sarva-bhāvena — sarva — whole, entire (first compound member); bhāva — being, state (sarva-bhāva: 'with one's whole being', instr. sg.)
glossary.भारत: bhārata — Bhārata — descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.इति: iti — iti — thus (particle, referring back to the whole preceding teaching)
glossary.गुह्यतमं: guhyatamam — guhya — secret, hidden (guhyatama: superlative, 'most secret', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with śāstram)
glossary.शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं: śāstram idam uktam — śāstra — teaching, scripture, doctrine (nom. sg. neut., subject; simply joined with idam); idam — this (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with śāstram; simply joined with uktam); vac — declared, spoken (ukta: past participle, uktam: nom. sg. neut., predicate, agreeing with śāstram)
glossary.मयानघ: mayā anagha — aham — I (mayā: instr. sg., 'by me'; mayā+anagha→mayānagha, ā+a→ā); an-agha — blameless, sinless (anagha: vocative sg., epithet of Arjuna)
glossary.एतद्बुद्ध्वा: etat buddhvā — etad — this (etat: acc. sg. neut., object of buddhvā, referring to the guhyatamam śāstram; etat+buddhvā→etadbuddhvā, -t+b-→-d b-); budh — to understand, know (buddhvā: gerund, 'having understood')
glossary.बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च: buddhimān syāt kṛta-kṛtyaḥ ca — buddhimant — possessing intellect, wise (buddhimān: nom. sg. masc., subject; simply joined with syāt); as — to be (syāt: optative 3rd sg., 'would become'); kṛta-kṛtya — one who has accomplished what was to be done, one whose purpose is fulfilled (bahuvrīhi; kṛtakṛtyaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate, in apposition with buddhimān; -aḥ+c-→-aś c-); ca — and

about: Chapter 15, the Yoga of the Supreme Person (Puruṣottamayoga), opens the poem's final stretch of teaching with the celebrated image of an inverted cosmic tree: an eternal aśvattha whose root grows upward and whose branches spread downward, nourished by the three guṇas, its leaves the hymns of the Veda, its lower roots binding human beings to action. Kṛṣṇa urges that this tree of transmigratory existence be felled with the firm weapon of non-attachment, so that the seeker may reach the imperishable state beyond the light of sun, moon and fire from which there is no return — his own supreme abode. He then turns to the individual soul, an eternal fragment of himself that enters a body, draws the senses to itself, and passes from body to body carrying them along as the wind carries scent away from a flower, unseen by the deluded but perceived by those with the eye of knowledge. A further set of verses identifies Kṛṣṇa with the hidden powers that sustain the natural world: the light in the sun, moon and fire; the vigor that upholds the earth and its creatures; the sap-giving Soma that nourishes the plants; the digestive fire in every living body; and the presence seated in the heart of all beings as the source of memory, knowledge, and their loss, at once the object, the author and the knower of the Veda. The chapter reaches its doctrinal climax with the teaching that gives it its name: two Persons exist in the world, the Perishable, which is every finite, changing being, and the unchanging Imperishable; but beyond both stands a third and highest Person, the Supreme Self, who pervades and sustains the three worlds — and this Supreme Person, Kṛṣṇa declares, he himself is. Whoever knows him thus, undeluded, as the Supreme Person, becomes a knower of all things and worships him with his whole being. The chapter closes with Kṛṣṇa naming this teaching the most secret of all, and promising that whoever understands it becomes wise and has accomplished everything that life requires.
